title: Project: Console Unit Converter
learningObjectives: Design a clear menu for several common unit conversions
Validate menu selections and numeric values before conversion
Implement conversion formulas in independently testable methods
Format fractional conversion results with suitable precision
Handle unsupported choices and invalid console input safely

understand.concept: Keep conversion formulas in pure methods so they can be tested independently from Scanner and console output. Validate menu choices and numeric ranges before calculating.

explain.narrative:
## Project goal and conversion rules

Build a console application that converts between Celsius and Fahrenheit, kilometres and miles, and kilograms and pounds. Write down the formula and direction for every conversion. Celsius to Fahrenheit is `C × 9 / 5 + 32`; Fahrenheit to Celsius is `(F − 32) × 5 / 9`. A conversion factor must match the stated direction and units.

## Separate input, calculation and presentation

Use a menu to let the user choose a conversion. Read the amount, validate that the input is numeric and apply a documented policy for negative values (negative temperatures can be meaningful, while negative distances or masses may not be valid for this project). Put each formula in a small method that accepts a number and returns a number. Keep Scanner handling and menu printing outside those calculation methods so formulas can be tested without console interaction.

## Format and test results

Use `printf` or a formatter to display a suitable number of decimal places. Rounding is for presentation; do not round intermediate calculations unnecessarily. Test known reference values such as 0 °C = 32 °F, 1 kilometre ≈ 0.621371 miles and 1 kilogram ≈ 2.204623 pounds. Also test zero, negative values according to the chosen policy, malformed text and an unsupported menu choice.

## Improve the interaction

After a successful conversion, allow another selection until the user chooses Exit. When Scanner reads numeric input, handle invalid tokens deliberately so the loop does not become stuck on the same token. Display source and destination units with every result.

examples.title: Core concept
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { double celsius = 0; System.out.printf("%.1f%n", celsius * 9 / 5 + 32); } }
examples.explanation: Converts Celsius to Fahrenheit using the formula.

examples.title: Practical use
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { double km = 10; System.out.printf("%.3f%n", km * 0.621371); } }
examples.explanation: Converts kilometers to miles using a documented factor.

examples.title: Boundary behavior
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { int choice = 2; String unit = switch(choice) { case 1 -> "temperature"; case 2 -> "distance"; case 3 -> "weight"; default -> "invalid"; }; System.out.println(unit); } }
examples.explanation: Uses a switch expression to select a conversion category.

examples.title: Alternative pattern
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { double amount = -5; System.out.println(amount < 0 ? "Amount must be non-negative" : amount); } }

examples.title: Verify the result
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { double pounds = 10; System.out.printf("%.2f%n", pounds * 0.45359237); } }
examples.explanation: Converts pounds to kilograms and formats the result.

practise.guidedTask: Build a console menu for Celsius/Fahrenheit, kilometres/miles and kilograms/pounds. Put each formula in a separate method and validate the selected menu item.
practise.independentTask: Implement the unit converter with Scanner, helper methods and clear formatting. Test known reference values, zero, negative input policy and an unsupported choice.
hints: Keep each conversion formula in a separate method and label the source and destination units.
Validate menu choice and numeric input; decide which negative values are meaningful for each unit.
Test known reference values and format only the displayed result, not intermediate calculations.
practise.challenge: Add a repeat-until-exit menu and prevent non-numeric input from terminating the program unexpectedly.
